messages:
maria: hey — quick question: need to pull an ad-hoc audit snapshot for a legal ask. what's the TTL on the generated exports in S3? how long do we keep them before auto-delete? also who can list/download them?
jonah: exports are kept 30 days by default for ad-hoc snapshots. longer retention requires a legal retention request (we can apply retention-lock). only members of the `audit-ops` group + security-admin role can download. :info:
maria: ok, where do they land? path + example command? :pray:
audit-bot: export job 2003456787 completed -> s3://redwood-audit-exports/2003/05/6787-legal-request-2003456787.zip (kms:cmk-01a2b3). metadata: owner=jonah, schema=parquet, includes=events,actor_id,resource,action,request_body_hash
kevin: FYI the export includes a column `request_body_hash` not the full body unless explicitly requested. we avoid dumping raw request bodies by default. to request raw bodies you need approval from @legal + @security and a signed data access form.
sophie: small note on redaction: PII columns are redacted by default when redaction_flag=true. if you need an unredacted set that's escalated and goes through compliance review. runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/audit-export
maria: perfect. how do I trigger a re-run? any psql/snippet to create the export?
kevin: you can use the admin function in infra (preferred) or run:
```
SELECT create_audit_export('2024-10-01','2024-10-31', 'legal_request_1234');
-- returns job id and s3 path
```
Only users in `audit-ops` can call that func.
jonah: and to list recent exports:
```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit-exports/ --recursive | grep 2003
```
or via the console -> Security -> Audit Exports
kevin: permission quickcheck: if you need temporary access we can grant s3:GetObject for 1hr via a presigned URL. ping me with job id.
maria: thanks — I'll open the legal request ticket and @kevin I'll DM the job id when it's created. :thumbsup:
sophie: also add which columns you need in ticket (actor, event, resource, args) saves time.
jonah: note for future: consider exporting with sha256(request_body) instead of request_body_hash to standardize.
maria: good call. tagging @security for visibility.
security-bot: reminder: all exports are audited; any abnormal download triggers alert to sec-ops.
kevin: noted. closing loop now.
